text.label: Heading: It works on anything. That's why we're showing it to you.
text.value: It works on anything. That's why we're showing it to you.

text.label: Text: You are a coach, an author or an influencer, and this page s
text.value: You are a coach, an author or an influencer, and this page shows you a truck bed builder, a pet wash and a firewood company. You are right to wonder what any of that has to do with you. Here is what you are looking at. These eight are demo sites. My team and I built every one of them to show how we build. Each one is live, which means you can open it on your own phone and use it the way a customer would, instead of looking at a picture of a website and guessing how it feels. They are here for one reason. I want you to judge the build with your own eyes before you ever talk to us.

text.label: Text: Every website has one job.
Text: A stranger shows up. They need to understand who you are and
text.value: A stranger shows up. They need to understand who you are and what you do without having to work for it. Then they need one clear next step. That is the whole job, and it does not change with what is being sold. A dog groomer needs it. A realtor needs it. A coach with 10,000 followers needs it more than either of them, because your stranger arrives off a clip, curious for about a minute, and leaves if the page does not meet them. They do not write to tell you why they left. You never find out they were there. So when you open a demo, do not ask yourself whether you care about firewood or truck beds. Ask whether a person who has never heard of that business could land on the page cold and know where they are before they lose interest. That is the test your own website has to pass, every day, with every follower who taps your name.

text.label: Text: Why these are so different.
Text: If we showed you eight coaching websites, you would judge th
text.value: If we showed you eight coaching websites, you would judge the coaching. You would compare their programs to yours and miss the point. So we show you businesses that have nothing in common with each other. Truck beds, paint correction, landscape design, water filtration, home repairs, real estate. When the work is that different and the page still does its job every time, the only thing left to look at is the build. That is what you would be buying from us. And if you want to see one built for a person who sells what they know, you are already on it. This website is the ninth example. It has a book for sale, a podcast and an application on it, and it is the one that runs my own company. Open the eight to judge the build. Look around this one to see what yours will carry.

text.label: Text: Open one on your phone.
Text: Start there, because that is where your audience lives. Some
text.value: Start there, because that is where your audience lives. Somebody watches a clip of you, taps your name and lands on your website with the phone still in their hand. Notice how the page fills the screen. Notice whether you have to pinch, zoom or hunt for anything. Run your thumb down the page the way you scroll everything else and see if it ever fights you. Most websites were built for a desk and squeezed onto a phone afterward, and you can feel it the second you land on one. The words are tiny. The button is off to the side somewhere. You give up. Yours will be built for the phone first, because that is how a follower will meet you, standing in a line with one free hand and a short supply of patience.

text.label: Text: Before you scroll at all, ask yourself two things. Do I know
text.value: Before you scroll at all, ask yourself two things. Do I know what this business does? Do I know who it is for? If the answer is yes, the page has done the hardest part of its job, and it did it before you moved your thumb. Try it on two or three of them. A water filtration company and a pet wash have nothing to say to each other, and each one still tells you where you are right away. Now picture your own name up there, with what you teach said that plainly. Who you help. What you help them do. Most people in your position have never had one place online that says it straight. They have a profile, a link and a hope.

text.label: Text: Look for the next step.
Text: Look at what each of these pages asks the visitor to do, and
text.value: Look at what each of these pages asks the visitor to do, and how easy it is to find. It is not hidden at the bottom, and it is not one of nine choices. A follower who has to guess what to do next does nothing, and they do not come back to try again. That is the quiet way attention gets wasted. Nobody complains. They just leave. On your website that step is buying what you know or getting on your calendar, and it sits where a thumb can reach it without a search. The demos show you how plain it should be. Nobody should need directions to give you money.

text.label: Text: Open the firewood company, then open the real estate site ri
text.value: Open the firewood company, then open the real estate site right after it. Ask yourself whether you would ever guess the same team built both. One is selling firewood to homes and barbecue restaurants. The other is selling a house. The colors, the pictures and the way each page talks belong to that one business and nobody else. That is what I mean when I say a website is built around one person. We do not have a house style that every client gets poured into. Yours will look and sound like you, with your face, your story and your words on it. My team does the building. The visitor only ever sees you.

text.label: Text: Now put yourself on one of those screens. Your face is at th
text.value: Now put yourself on one of those screens. Your face is at the top, with one line under it that says who you help and what you help them do. Below that is your own e-book, with your name on the cover and a button to buy it. Below that is your own show, ready to play. Then one clear way to get on your calendar. A stranger who met you in a clip a minute ago can now read you, hear you and pay you without leaving the page. Everything you put out on the social platforms sits on rented land. This page is the piece you own, and every clip, every episode and every mention of your name sends people to it. Open two or three of the demos. Then come back, because for you the website is only where it starts.

text.label: Heading: For you, the website is only the front door.
text.value: For you, the website is only the front door.

text.label: Text: Everything above is the first of six systems, the website. F
text.value: Everything above is the first of six systems, the website. For the businesses in those demos, that page sells a service: a clean truck, a repaired fence, a house. The visitor already knows they need the thing. The page only has to show them who to call. Yours has a harder job, because you are not selling a service somebody can look up. You are selling what you know, and a stranger does not know they need it until they have spent some time with you. So your website carries two things you will not find on any of the eight, and it sits in front of something a demo cannot show you at all.

text.label: Text: Go back to any demo and find the spot where the page asks fo
text.value: Go back to any demo and find the spot where the page asks for the business. On yours, that spot sells your own e-book. Here is why it has to exist. Most people with an audience have never sat down and turned what they know into something a person can buy. It stays in their head, in their videos and in their answers to messages, handed out one reply at a time for nothing. My team and I pull it out of you and package it into your own e-book, with your name on the cover, sold on your website. Now a follower who likes you has a way to pay you without waiting for you to answer them personally. It is the easiest thing on the page to say yes to, and the person who buys it is no longer just watching.

text.label: Text: None of these eight has a show on it. Yours will. We produce
text.value: None of these eight has a show on it. Yours will. We produce it and it lives on your website, just like mine does on this one. Here is why it matters. People need to see you and hear from you seven to ten times before they trust you enough to pay. A page on a website gets a visitor for a minute or two. A podcast is how they spend real time with you, in their car and in their kitchen, over and over, until your voice is familiar. You talk about what you know. We handle the editing, the publishing and the rest of the technical work that stops most people from ever starting one. When you scroll back up to those demos, picture a play button on the page with your voice behind it.

text.label: Text: That is a talent agency.
Text: Packaging what you know and getting you seen and heard is wh
text.value: Packaging what you know and getting you seen and heard is what a talent agent has always done. My team and I are a modern day talent agency, and the first thing an agent does for the talent is build the stage. Every demo you opened is a stage. It was built for one business, to put that business in front of a stranger and get the stranger to act. Yours gets built for one person, and that person is you. We show you how to promote yourself, and then my team does the heavy end of it for you. Self-promotion with nowhere to send people is just noise. A stage gives it somewhere to land.

text.label: Text: Here is what a demo cannot show you. You can see the page. Y
text.value: Here is what a demo cannot show you. You can see the page. You cannot see what happens after a visitor taps the button, and that is where the money is made. Behind your website sit the other five systems of the Revenue Engine, our own proprietary system, connected to the website and to each other. The Automated Organic Content Engine brings people in. Speed to Lead answers them in seconds. Automated Five Star Reviews collects your proof. CRM Mastery goes back to everyone who went quiet, which is where the cross-sells and upsells live. Paid ads are added last. That order never changes, because each system needs the one before it. It is one build at one price, and all six go in. We never sell it in pieces.

text.label: Text: A fair thing to ask after looking at eight finished websites
text.value: A fair thing to ask after looking at eight finished websites is who wrote all those words. My team did. On yours, we start by sitting down with you and getting you talking. Your story, who you help, what you teach and how you say it. Then my team writes the website from that, so it reads like you on a good day and not like a brochure. You talk, and my team turns it into finished pages. After it is live, AI employees do the answering and the following up, day and night, which is the part no person can keep up with for every follower. Behind those AI employees is my team, a US company with real people on the work, and I am personally on your account.

text.label: Text: You keep doing the thing that built your audience. During th
text.value: You keep doing the thing that built your audience. During the build, you sit down with us so we can get what you know out of your head, onto the website and into the e-book. Once it is running, your part comes down to four things that only you can do. You record, talking about what you know. You take the calls with people who are ready. You take care of your clients. And you look at your numbers, so you know what is working. We build the website, package the product, produce the podcast and connect the six systems. The answering, the following up and the asking for testimonials are handled. When a buyer is ready to talk, that conversation lands on your calendar.

text.label: Text: Everything in this half of the page is how my own company ru
text.value: Everything in this half of the page is how my own company runs. This website, my book, my podcast and the six systems behind them are the prototype. What a client gets is that same business model, front to back, with their name on it instead of mine. I mean that literally. You get the website, the list of people who raise a hand, your e-book, your podcast and the six systems, with AI employees working them day and night. Every video, clip and episode you put out sends people to that one address. That is the whole reason to build on a website you own. My team and I build every page of it to a standard I would put my own name on, and I do not see anybody else building a person the whole thing.

text.label: Text: Here is who this is built for. If having your own podcast an
text.value: Here is who this is built for. If having your own podcast and your own product scares you, we are not the right fit, and it is better you know that now. If you read this and thought, that is the piece I have been missing, there are three ways to work with us. Do it yourself is my book, the blueprint, $495.00, for the person with more time than money right now. Done with you is the Revenue Share Partnership, $3,995.00 to start. It is how a modern day talent agency gets behind a person with something to say and an audience already listening. Done for you is $40,000.00 to $60,000.00, for the person who already sells what they know and has a small team in place. We work with 5 to 10 of those clients at a time. In those two, you get the same website, your own e-book, your own podcast and all six systems, with my team and AI employees working them day and night, so what you know starts earning the way it should. Every client starts with a discovery call, and that is where you get your exact price. The application is one tap from here.

text.value: Tell us who you help and what you sell, and we will set up the discovery call.
